article_title: What failure of COP31 reveals about a divided world
adaptation_summary: Adapted for level C; emphasis on article-specific comprehension, vocabulary in context, and concise written responses.

tasks.prompt: What does the article argue COP31's failure mainly reveals?
options: Climate science is no longer accepted by any government
International climate action is constrained by deep geopolitical, fossil-fuel and finance divisions
Solar technology has stopped improving
The UN has already replaced consensus with majority voting
tasks.correct_answer: International climate action is constrained by deep geopolitical, fossil-fuel and finance divisions
tasks.explanation_hebrew: הכתבה טוענת שכישלון COP31 משקף פערים עמוקים באינטרסים גיאופוליטיים, בדלקי מאובנים ובמימון אקלים.

tasks.prompt: Approximately how many governments backed explicit language on moving away from fossil fuels?
options: Twenty-two governments
Nearly every government present
About 130 governments
Only the European Union
tasks.explanation_hebrew: כ־130 ממשלות, בערך שני שלישים מהמדינות שהשתתפו, תמכו בניסוח מפורש על מעבר מדלקי מאובנים.

tasks.prompt: What was unusual about the proposed Antalya Pact compared with the COP28 agreement?
options: It omitted any mention of fossil fuels after COP28 had agreed to transition away from them
It required every country to stop using electricity
It replaced climate finance with military aid
It set a lower global temperature target than 1.5°C
tasks.correct_answer: It omitted any mention of fossil fuels after COP28 had agreed to transition away from them
tasks.explanation_hebrew: ב־COP28 הוסכם לעבור מדלקי מאובנים, ואילו טיוטת אנטליה לא הזכירה אותם כלל.

tasks.prompt: What does “unbridgeable red lines” mean in Bowen's description of the negotiations?
options: Temporary translation problems
Minor disagreements about meeting rooms
Targets that all sides had already accepted
Firm and incompatible positions that could not be reconciled
tasks.correct_answer: Firm and incompatible positions that could not be reconciled
tasks.explanation_hebrew: הביטוי מתאר עמדות יסוד קשיחות וסותרות שלא ניתן היה לגשר ביניהן.

tasks.prompt: Why did Russia's delegate oppose language on cutting fossil fuels?
options: He warned that reducing supply before demand fell could cause shortages, higher prices and energy poverty
He said Arab countries caused most historical emissions
He wanted the US to lead the talks
He argued that solar panels were too competitive
tasks.correct_answer: He warned that reducing supply before demand fell could cause shortages, higher prices and energy poverty
tasks.explanation_hebrew: הנציג הרוסי טען שקיצוץ בהיצע לפני ירידה בביקוש עלול לגרום למחסור, עליית מחירים ועוני אנרגטי.

tasks.prompt: Why might majority voting produce a strong agreement on paper but weak action in practice?
options: Voting would automatically end renewable investment
The agreement would apply only to small nations
Countries that were outvoted might not voluntarily implement commitments they rejected
The UN could legally force every government to comply
tasks.correct_answer: Countries that were outvoted might not voluntarily implement commitments they rejected
tasks.explanation_hebrew: שיתוף הפעולה הבינלאומי הוא ברובו וולונטרי, ולכן מדינות שהפסידו בהצבעה עלולות לא ליישם את ההסכם.

tasks.prompt: Identify two ways the broader political context weakened the Antalya negotiations.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש לציין שני פרטים: היעדר משלחת אמריקאית רשמית ודחיית טראמפ את תהליך האקלים; או ההצהרה המשותפת של ארה״ב, סין ורוסיה להגדיל מוצרי נפט מזוקק.
expected_points: The United States sent no official delegation, although it had previously helped broker compromises.
President Trump rejected the international climate process.
Trump, Xi and Putin issued a declaration supporting increased production and supply of refined petroleum products while COP delegates debated fossil fuels.

tasks.prompt: Why do many developing countries object to the way climate finance is provided?
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש להסביר שחלק גדול מהמימון ניתן כהלוואות ולא כמענקים, כך שהמדינות העניות מחזירות סכומים גדולים, אף שתרומתן ההיסטורית לנזק הייתה קטנה והן זקוקות לעזרה להסתגל.
expected_points: Much climate finance arrives as loans rather than grants.
Developing countries may repay more than they receive.
They argue they contributed little to the historical problem but are being asked to pay for the damage.
They say assistance is insufficient for adaptation and cleaner development.

tasks.prompt: Write 3–4 sentences evaluating Christiana Figueres's view that countries were right to reject a weaker pact.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש לשקול את ההגנה על התחייבות COP28 ואת תמיכת הרוב מול המחיר של סיום הפסגה ללא הצהרה מוסכמת.
expected_points: Rejecting the pact protected the earlier COP28 commitment to move away from fossil fuels.
About 130 governments supported stronger explicit language, so the rejection represented a substantial majority.
Accepting a vague emissions promise might have weakened political pressure on fossil-fuel use.
However, walking away also meant losing a declaration that contained strong warnings about exceeding 1.5°C.

tasks.prompt: Summarise why COP31 failed, why consensus is difficult to replace and what continues outside the talks in 4–5 sentences.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש לכלול את המחלוקות על דלקי מאובנים ומימון, ההקשר הגיאופוליטי, היתרונות והחסרונות של קונצנזוס, והמשך המעבר האנרגטי בקצב איטי מדי.
expected_points: The Antalya Pact collapsed over explicit fossil-fuel language, climate finance and competing national interests.
Oil-producing countries defended their right to choose their transition path, while many governments refused to weaken the COP28 commitment.
The absence of US leadership and wider geopolitical divisions made compromise harder.
Consensus can block ambition, but it also supports voluntary implementation and protects smaller countries from being overruled.
Renewables, batteries and electric vehicles continue to advance, although the article says the transition remains too slow for the climate.
